The minutes of a meeting held 3 May 1834, approving a change in the name of the church, include an attestation that the church was originally organized 6 April 1830 in Fayette. JS and Oliver Cowdery both signed the minutes. The deed of purchase for church lands in Ohio likewise identified Fayette and was signed by Oliver Cowdery. (“Communicated,”The Evening and the Morning Star,May 1834, 160; Geauga Co., OH, Deed Records, 1795–1921, vol. 18, pp. 478–479, 5 May 1834, microfilm 20,237, U.S. and Canada Record Collection, FHL.)
Oliver Cowdery later crossed out “1829” and inserted “Ap[r]il 1830.” Still later, John Whitmer inserted “6” to make the date “Ap[r]il 6 1830.”

In the Book of Mormon, Jesus’s twelve disciples “were called the Elders of the church.” (Book of Mormon, 1830 ed., 575 [Moroni 3:1].)

Cowdery was one of two presiding elders in the new Church of Christ, second in authority to JS. JS and Cowdery used the titles “first Elder” and “second Elder,” respectively, in signing ministerial licenses. (See License for John Whitmer, License for Joseph Smith Sr., License for Christian Whitmer, 9 June 1830, inJSP,D1:142–150.)
According to JS’s history, Oliver Cowdery had already been ordained an elder of the church by the time JS dictated this revelation. (JS History, vol. A-1, 37, inJSP,H1:366 [Draft 2].)

On Sunday, 11 April 1830, at Fayette, “Oliver Cowdery preached the first public discourse, that was delivered by any of our number. … Large numbers of people attended” and Cowdery baptized several people. The baptisms took place in Seneca Lake near the Whitmer farm. (See JS History, vol. A-1, 39, inJSP,H1:378 [Draft 2].)

David Whitmer, one of the few attendees who wrote about the event, stated: “We attended to our business of organizing, according to the laws of the land, the church acknowledging us six elders as their ministers; besides, a few who had recently been baptized and not confirmed were confirmed on that day; some blessings were pronounced, and we partook of the Lord’s supper.” (Whitmer,Address to All Believers in Christ,33.)
